title: Follow-ups: the next size up past a product's first page, the item checked against its order, halves that stay live, a saved draft told truly, and the order tests made able to fail
requested_outcome:
Ten follow-ups from the round-12 deploy review, filed as work for the next build under the owner's ship rule of 30 September, around making a new order by voice, the halves of a conversation and a draft he asks CLIVE to forget. Fix each with a test that fails on the code at the base commit.
- S2Ba/F-03 (app/families/order_create.py VARIANT_SIBLINGS_QUERY, _read_product_of; app/families/_sizes.py step): only the first 100 of a product's variants are read and the starting variant's own options are dropped, so 'the next size up' says a variant or size does not exist when it lies past that page.
- S2Ba/F-04 (app/families/order_create.py ORDER_FOR_NEW_ORDER_QUERY, _fill_opened, _step_size): with both order_id and variant_id given, the source order is read but the variant is never checked against its lines, so a variant of an unrelated product is stepped; the source order's lines are read only to the first 20.
- S2Bb/S2Bb-03 (app/routes/branches.py merge, background, focus): /merge lets the only live, focused half be merged, leaving no live half; /background can turn a merged or cancelled half back to BACKGROUND, after which /focus makes it ACTIVE again.
- S2b/S2b-04 (app/families/compose.py _latest_draft, _draft_discard): draft.discard on a draft already saved in Gmail (VERIFIED) withdraws nothing and still answers 'Forgotten. Nothing was saved.'. Say truly that the draft is saved in Gmail; do not delete it (deleting from Gmail is a write and not this build's).
- X1/X1-03 (experience/scenario_packs/commerce.py order_by_voice): the scenario calls its draft check exact but asserts only the lines, postcode and total, so a wrong or missing customer and email, or different postage, would pass.
- T1/T1-03 (tests/test_r12_orders.py): order 2102's date is built as '2026-09--1T10:00:00Z'.
- T7/T7-02 (tests/test_r12_orders_browser.py): the fake draftOrderComplete answers #1999 on every call and nothing counts completions, so a second completion would go unseen.
- T2/F-03 (tests/test_r12_surfaces.py, the refused-note test): it checks only that the order stays on screen, so it would pass if a note for order 9999 were staged or no reason were given.
- T2/F-01 (tests/test_r12_surfaces.py, the on-screen-claim test): it leaves a NullTimeline installed rather than restoring the timeline it displaced.
- R9-I-tests2-I-02 (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; tests/test_turn_boundary.py, tests/test_r11_turn.py): with another record in focus, the order and named-person tests accept the answer 'Here it is.', which names neither the record asked for nor a refusal.
A new order is still only a draft until the owner's hold; which item or order is meant is the model's choice from his words, and the code checks what it chose.

What must not change, in every part of this build: every sentence the owner types or says still goes to the model exactly as said, and nothing here reads, answers or routes a sentence by a word list in front of it (deterministic code may check what the model did, never decide for it); every change to the shop or to email stays behind the owner's hold-to-confirm card, nothing here adds a write or skips staging, confirmation or verification, and reads stay reads; no private business data goes into git, and every name, address and order in a test is invented; no test assertion is weakened (an assertion changed here is made stricter, and the report names each one); the kernel, the gate, secret scanning and the acceptance machinery are untouched, and no protected path is edited (protected tests such as tests/test_compose.py, tests/test_engineering_bridge.py and tests/conftest.py are run, never changed); docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md is regenerated by the loop and never edited by hand. Plain British English in comments and docstrings that say what is true and why; no placeholder copy, invented defaults or filler.

The previous attempt stopped because failing closed when pageInfo.hasNextPage is missing made the golden check fail: experience/fixtures/shopify.py's _variant_siblings answered the product-variants connection without pageInfo. That file is now in scope for exactly that: each connection the fixture answers for these reads carries pageInfo {hasNextPage: false, endCursor: null} beside its edges, as Shopify does. Change nothing else in the fixture. If the branch clive/objective/followups-orders-drafts-halves is in your workspace, its last commit is a near-complete version of this work.
acceptance_criteria: S2Ba/F-03: with a fake product whose variants run past the first page (hasNextPage and a cursor), the next size up is found when the starting variant or the target size is past the first page; a read cut short by its bound refuses and says the read was incomplete, never that the size does not exist; the starting variant's options come from its own lookup.

S2Ba/F-04: shopify_order_open with an order_id and a variant_id on none of that order's lines is refused with a plain reason naming the order, and nothing is added to the workspace; a variant that is on a line still steps as today; a source order whose lines run past the first page is paged or refused as incomplete, never stepped from a partial read.

S2Bb-03: /merge on the only live half is refused (409) and the half stays live and focused; /merge and /background on a MERGED or CANCELLED half are refused and its status is unchanged; no sequence of /background, /focus and /merge makes a merged or cancelled half live again.

S2b-04: draft.discard on a VERIFIED draft answers that the draft is saved in Gmail and was not deleted, withdraws nothing and makes no Gmail call; on a PENDING draft it still withdraws the card and answers 'Forgotten. Nothing was saved.'; tests/test_compose.py (protected, unchanged) still passes.

X1-03: order_by_voice asserts that exactly one draft was created in the fixture shop and that it carries the found customer's id and email, the source order's whole shipping address and the postage asked for, beside its existing line, discount and total checks; tests/test_experience.py -k order_by_voice passes.
T1-03: the fixture dates in tests/test_r12_orders.py are made by date arithmetic; order 2102 has a valid 2026-08-30 timestamp, asserted in a test, and the tests that read it still pass.
T7-02: the browser test's fake completion counts its calls; the test asserts exactly one after the hold and none after the attempted repeat, and an unexpected second call fails it.
T2/F-03: the refused-note test also asserts that the note call was refused, no proposal is pending, no mutation reached the fake shop, and the response gives the owner a reason.
T2/F-01: the on-screen-claim test saves the timeline it displaces and restores exactly that one in its finally.

R9-I-tests2-I-02: those turn tests script an answer that names the record asked for, and assert that the answer the owner hears names it and that the card and the cursor are that record; none passes with 'Here it is.'.
The new tests are in tests/test_followups_orders.py, each failing on the base code; the order, branch, compose, surfaces and turn tests and tests/test_r13_evidence_index.py still pass.
